summary: Request: guidance on break-glass override for offline bundle signature verification (air-gapped Redwood Private install)
description:
Issue summary
GovLab Research is preparing an air-gapped Redwood Private upgrade. Their internal security team requested a formal, step-by-step process for using the installer “break-glass” override if signature verification blocks the install, including:
- Who at Redwood must approve (and what evidence we provide)
- What the customer must record locally (commands/logs/audit events)
- How to remediate after the emergency install to return to normal verification

Context
- Customer is in a strict air-gapped environment with controlled media transfer and change-management gates.
- They anticipate possible verification failure due to: time skew, trust store not yet updated after key rotation, or media transfer corruption.
- They do NOT want a generic ‘use --insecure’ instruction; they need a documented, auditable exception path.

Customer request
1) Provide the official Redwood approval path for break-glass verification override.
2) Provide required logs and artifacts to capture for audit.
3) Provide a follow-up checklist to restore normal verification (including trust store update and re-validation).

Notes
This is guidance-only (no active install failure reported yet). Customer wants this before their change window next week.

Proposed guidance to provide (draft)
A) Preconditions (before considering break-glass)
- Confirm bundle integrity on the staging workstation BEFORE transfer (sha256 checks on the bundle archive and manifest).
- Run installer inspect/verify commands to capture failure reason.
- Attempt standard remediations: correct clock/time source, update trust store, re-transfer media, re-extract with supported tools.

B) Break-glass approval path (Redwood)
- Support opens SUP ticket + attaches verification output and customer change window timeline.
- Required Redwood approvals:
  - Security Eng sign-off: Marcus Lin (or delegate) confirms failure mode and that break-glass is appropriate.
  - GRC/Policy sign-off: Olga Petrov (or delegate) confirms exception logging requirements.
  - Exec sponsor for exceptions (as needed): Dr. Aisha Rahman for high-risk or repeated exceptions.
- Support/SE provide customer a written statement documenting: reason, scope (bundle build id/version), timeframe, and required follow-up.

C) Break-glass execution (customer)
- Run installer preflight in verbose mode and capture output.
- Run install with the policy-gated break-glass flag (exact flag name depends on installer version; customer must be on the minimum installer version that supports auditable override).
- Ensure local audit log retention is enabled; verify the override emits an explicit audit marker event.

D) Required artifacts/logs to capture (customer)
- Full output of:
  - bundle inspection/verify command
  - preflight command
  - install command (with flags; redact tokens if any)
- Installer logs from the documented log path
- Generated support bundle (must include bundle metadata + verification status)
- Local audit events for:
  - bundle_verification_failed (with reason)
  - bundle_verification_break_glass_used
  - install_started/install_completed

E) Follow-up to restore normal verification
- Update installer trust store to include current signing root(s) (air-gapped transfer) and confirm key IDs.
- Re-run verify against the same bundle offline; confirm signature validates without override.
- For the next upgrade, block using break-glass by default (policy reset) and document closure of the exception in change records.

Acceptance criteria for closing this ticket
- Customer confirms they received:
  - Approval matrix + escalation contacts
  - Required logs list
  - Post-exception remediation checklist
- Support has an internal checklist ready to reuse for similar requests.
comments: 2026-01-29 10:14 PT — Dev Patel (Reporter): GovLab Research asking for documented break-glass process for air-gapped upgrades. They’re not currently failing verification; they want the procedure approved by security/GRC before their change window. Assigning to Owen for response + aligning with Security (Marcus) and GRC (Olga).

2026-01-29 11:02 PT — Owen Phillips (Assignee): Acknowledged. I’ll draft customer-facing steps + internal approval matrix. Will confirm minimum installer version that supports auditable break-glass and what audit events we expect to see locally.

2026-01-29 13:26 PT — Marcus Lin (Security Eng): For guidance: emphasize we fail closed by default; break-glass is only for time-bound exception with explicit audit marker. Require customer to capture verify output and reason codes. If failure reason is “unknown key”, they must update trust store ASAP; break-glass should not be used as a long-term workaround for key rotation.

2026-01-29 14:10 PT — Olga Petrov (GRC): Add: customer should retain local logs for their standard change-management retention period; Redwood will provide a short exception memo stating scope (bundle build id/version/hash), reason, and follow-up actions. For repeated usage, route to Aisha for exec-level review.

2026-01-30 09:18 PT — Owen Phillips: Sent GovLab the ‘Break-glass override procedure’ draft via email and attached it to the ticket. Included (1) decision tree before break-glass, (2) Redwood approval contacts and required sign-offs, (3) exact artifacts/logs to collect, (4) follow-up steps to restore normal verification. Also included note that they must be on the minimum installer version that emits the break-glass audit event and includes verification status in the support bundle.

2026-01-30 09:44 PT — Colin O'Donnell (Solutions Eng): Adding that GovLab uses offline Windows jump hosts for media prep; we should remind them to avoid extraction tools that can alter file contents/line endings. Referenced our prior guidance from SUP-31892 (hash mismatch after transfer).

2026-02-03 16:07 PT — Owen Phillips: Customer confirmed receipt and that the approval matrix/log requirements meet their internal security review checklist. No break-glass executed yet. Closing as resolved; if they hit an actual verification failure during the window, we’ll open a new incident-style ticket with logs attached.
resolution: Provided customer-facing break-glass override procedure including: (1) preconditions and standard remediation steps before override, (2) Redwood approval path (Support + Security Eng + GRC; exec review if repeated/high risk), (3) required logs/support bundle/audit events to capture locally, and (4) follow-up checklist to restore normal signature verification (trust store update + re-verify without override). Customer confirmed the process satisfies their change-management requirements.
next_steps: If GovLab experiences an actual verification block during the change window, open a new SUP ticket and attach: bundle verify output, installer logs, and support bundle. Route to Security Eng if break-glass is requested for an “unknown key” reason; prefer trust store update and re-verify. Track repeated break-glass usage for exec review per policy.
